walkthroughs.body_html:
Introduction to Religions (Two from: Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, Baha'i, Jainism, Taoism, Indigenous Religions) — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Introduction to Religions (Two from: Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Sikhism, Baha'i, Jainism, Taoism, Indigenous Religions) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: How does Reform Judaism differ from Orthodox Judaism?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

Reform Judaism treats Jewish law (halakhah) as evolving and not strictly binding, embraces modernity, and grants gender equality; Orthodox Judaism holds halakhah as divinely given and binding in detail, with traditional practice maintained.
Orthodox Judaism is a different religion from Reform Judaism.
Reform Jews don't believe in God and Orthodox Jews do.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Orthodox Judaism is a different religion from Reform Judaism.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was half God and half human.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
